g.text: Two ways to lay a hash table out in memory (8 buckets, 4 keys, load factor 0.5)
A. separate chaining: an array of pointers; entries live in separately allocated list nodes
Every hop is a pointer chase into a separate
heap allocation, so each hop can miss cache.
B. open addressing: entries live in the array itself; a collision walks to the next slot
a deleted key leaves a tombstone so
later probes do not stop early
Neighboring slots share cache lines and there
is no pointer chasing, but the table must
resize before alpha gets close to 1.
